summary.intent: Identify and fix slow unit test bottlenecks in the CLI repo, addressing them one at a time with user review between each fix.
summary.outcome: Two test performance fixes landed on PR #830: isolated TestListSessionsFunctionsWithoutRepo in a temp non-repo dir (~4s → ~0.01s) and reduced external agent timeout test deadlines from 1s to 200ms with adjusted upper bounds (2s→4s after PR review feedback). P1 opencode tests were investigated but reverted due to approach disagreements.

repo: TestListSessionsFunctionsWithoutRepo in cmd/entire/cli/strategy/session_test.go was running from the real repo CWD, causing ~4s runtime by scanning the actual repo; a t.TempDir()+t.Chdir fix reduces it to ~0.01s

cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode lifecycle tests (TestPrepareTranscript_*) invoke real opencode export path, making them ~1.1s each — but fixing this via injectable function fields on production structs or t.Setenv/t.Chdir are both unacceptable approaches
run() in external agent sets cmd.WaitDelay = 3*time.Second, so elapsed upper bounds in timeout tests must be at least timeout + WaitDelay (e.g. 200ms + 3s) to avoid CI flakes
ENTIRE_TEST_OPENCODE_MOCK_EXPORT=1 is a mock mode for opencode export but requires t.Setenv which conflicts with t.Parallel — not usable for parallel tests

The opencode export slow-path tests cannot be easily mocked without either modifying production structs (rejected as 'too much production change') or using t.Setenv (rejected as incompatible with t.Parallel)

code.finding: TestListSessionsFunctionsWithoutRepo needed t.TempDir()+t.Chdir to avoid scanning real repo CWD
Elapsed upper bound raised from 2s to 4s to accommodate WaitDelay=3s in production run()
TestRun_RespectsExistingDeadline context timeout reduced from 1s to 200ms
Elapsed upper bound raised from 2s to 4s to accommodate WaitDelay=3s in production run()

workflow: PR was initially created for only one commit on a new branch instead of the full feature branch — user corrected to use fix/optimize-tests branch containing all changes
The task/review tool reported nothing when working tree was clean; it requires uncommitted or branch-scoped changes to be useful
Cursor bot PR comments flagged the WaitDelay flake risk and the fix was valid — worth checking bot review comments before merging
Reverting via git checkout -- <file> was used to cleanly undo uncommitted test changes

friction: Two rounds of P1 (opencode PrepareTranscript) approach were rejected: first t.Setenv+t.Chdir removed t.Parallel (unacceptable), then injectable exportSession field on production struct deemed 'too much production code change' — no viable path found without touching production code
PR was created on wrong branch (pr/external-timeout-tests) with only one commit instead of the full fix/optimize-tests branch; had to close #829 and reopen #830
The task/review tool was invoked twice mid-session but returned no useful output both times because the working tree was clean
Agent tried to merge brainstorming P-label numbering between sessions (P1 summarize Claude test vs P1 opencode test) causing confusion when user questioned the plan
open_items: TestPrepareTranscript_AlwaysRefreshesTranscript and TestPrepareTranscript_ErrorOnBrokenSymlink in cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/lifecycle_test.go still take ~1.1s each — no acceptable test-only fix found without production changes
TestGenerateFromTranscript_NilGenerator in cmd/entire/cli/summarize/summarize_test.go (~4.6s) was deferred as it depends on real claude CLI — still slow
cmd/entire/cli/strategy git-heavy reconcile tests (metadata_reconcile_test.go) remain ~12s aggregate — deeper optimization deferred as medium-hard effort
cmd/entire/cli package-level slowness (~9s) not investigated — no obvious single bottleneck identified yet
TestWrap_HooksAndAnalyzer refactor (pure in-memory Agent construction) was considered but reverted to preserve incidental integration coverage — could revisit if integration coverage moves elsewhere
